summary: Obfuscated date-parser exfiltrates form PII and loads remote script into host page
details: The package presents itself as a date parser but its sole exported function injects code into any page that uses it. On click of Ant Design primary modal buttons it reads firstName/age/address form inputs and transmits them as query parameters via fetch, and on beforeunload uses navigator.sendBeacon to POST base64-encoded data to a '/leak?data_stolen_on_unload_base64=' endpoint. The destination host is read from a page meta tag (fallback example.com). The same injected code loads an attacker-controlled script from '<host>/tag_added_via_script_import.js' via a runtime-constructed eval("import(...)") and an appended <script> tag, and uses new Function(...) and setInterval(eval(...)) as additional execution sinks, granting the meta-tag domain operator arbitrary script execution in the host page. Additional covert behaviors include reading and writing the user's clipboard and decoding an embedded ~97KB base64 blob into a Blob that is auto-clicked as a forced file download two seconds after use. The entire module is wrapped in obfuscator.io-style string-array + rotate + base64 obfuscation hiding the URLs, selectors, storage keys (literally named 'sendToUnload_secretData'), and eval strings. None of these behaviors match the advertised date-parsing purpose.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
